paper.title: Bandit Theory meets Compressed Sensing for high dimensional Stochastic Linear Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional sparse stochastic linear bandit on the unit l2 ball
unmapped: Noise is added to the parameter: r_t = <x_t, theta + eta_t> with eta_t an i.i.d. white-noise vector whose coordinates are independent and bounded |eta_{k,t}| <= sigma_k/2
High-dimensional regime: dimension K much larger than horizon n; sparsity S < n unknown to the learner
Learner knows upper bounds on ||theta||_2 and ||sigma||_2 (vector of coordinate noise ranges)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $1\leq t \leq n$ it selects an arm $x_t$ in the set of arms $\D_{K}$, which is the unit ball for the $||.||_2$-norm induced by the inner product. It then receives a reward $r_t = \langle x_t,\theta+\eta_t\rangle$, where $\eta_t\in \R^K$ is an i.i.d.~white noise ... we make the assumption that $\theta$ is $S-$sparse with $S<n$.

symbols.sigma_bar_2: known upper bound on ||sigma||_2, sigma the vector of per-coordinate noise ranges

conditions: Assumption 1: (eta_{k,t}) i.i.d. white noise with |eta_{k,t}| <= sigma_k/2
theta is S-sparse with S < n
holds with probability at least 1 - 5 delta
tuning: b = (bar theta_2 + bar sigma_2) sqrt(2 log(2K/delta))

source.label: thm:m1-regret
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{as:noise1}, if we choose $\bar{\sigma}_2 \geq ||\si||_2$, and $\bar{\theta}_2 \geq ||\theta||_2$, the regret of SL-UCB is bounded with probability at least $1-5\delta$, as $R_n(\Alg_{SL-UCB})\leq 118 (\bar{\theta}_2+ \bar{\sigma}_2)^2 \log(2K/\delta)S \sqrt{n}$.

results.notes: Paper's K is the dimension (d), n the horizon (T), S the sparsity (s_sparse). Regret is n||theta||_2 - sum_t <theta,x_t> (through means, but random actions), stated w.p. 1-5delta. Sparsity S not required by algorithm. Noise mapped to subgaussian since reward noise <x,eta> is bounded.
